title: Hudson Enters the Harbor
description: Henry Hudson, sailing the Halve Maen for the Dutch East India Company, enters the Upper Bay in mid-September and sails up the river that will carry his name.

title: First Dutch Settlers
description: The ship Nieu Nederlandt lands about thirty families, mostly Walloons, for the Dutch West India Company; a party camps on Noten Eylandt (Governors Island).

title: Fort Amsterdam Begun
description: The company's engineer Cryn Fredericks lays out a fort and a town at the tip of Manhattan; New Amsterdam grows around it.

title: Manhattan Changes Hands
description: Director Peter Minuit acquires Manhattan from the Lenape for goods worth 60 guilders, as a letter of 5 November 1626 by Pieter Schaghen reports.

title: Bronck's Land
description: Jonas Bronck settles on the mainland across the Harlem River; the river beside his farm, and later the borough, take his name.

title: Breuckelen
description: The village of Breuckelen on Long Island receives its own municipal government from the Dutch West India Company.

title: The Wall
description: New Amsterdam receives municipal rights on 2 February; that spring a palisade is built across the island against an English attack. The path along it becomes Wall Street.

title: Nieuw Haarlem
description: Director-General Peter Stuyvesant founds the village of Nieuw Haarlem on the flats of northern Manhattan.

title: Oude Dorp
description: Dutch and French-speaking families found Oude Dorp near South Beach, the first lasting European settlement on Staten Island.

title: New Amsterdam Becomes New York
description: An English squadron under Richard Nicolls arrives at the end of August; Stuyvesant surrenders the town without a shot in early September and it is renamed for the Duke of York.

title: New Orange
description: A Dutch fleet under Cornelis Evertsen retakes the city and renames it New Orange; the Treaty of Westminster returns it to England in November 1674.

title: The Counties
description: The Province of New York is divided into twelve counties, among them New York, Kings, Queens, Richmond and Westchester.

title: King's Bridge
description: A toll bridge owned by Frederick Philipse is built over Spuyten Duyvil Creek, carrying the Boston Post Road from Manhattan to the mainland.

title: Bowling Green
description: The Common Council leases the old parade ground before the fort for a bowling green, the city's first public park.

title: Battle of Long Island
description: British and Hessian troops turn the American lines on the heights of Brooklyn in the largest battle of the war; Washington ferries his army to Manhattan two nights later.

title: The Great Fire of 1776
description: Six days after the British take the city a fire starting near Whitehall Slip burns between 400 and 1,000 buildings, up to a quarter of the town, including Trinity Church.

title: Evacuation Day
description: The last British troops leave and Washington's army marches down to the Battery.

title: Capital of the United States
description: George Washington takes the oath of office at Federal Hall on Wall Street; New York is the national capital until 1790.

title: The Commissioners' Plan
description: The commissioners' map fixes a grid of twelve avenues and 155 cross streets over Manhattan north of Houston Street.

title: The Collect Is Filled
description: The Collect Pond, once the town's fresh water and by now polluted, is drained through a canal and filled; the Five Points slum rises on the sinking ground.

title: Steam Ferry to Brooklyn
description: Fulton's steam ferry Nassau begins crossing between Manhattan and Brooklyn, opening Brooklyn Heights to commuters.

title: The Erie Canal
description: The Erie Canal opens; the canal boat Seneca Chief reaches New York nine days later and Governor Clinton pours Lake Erie water into the harbor. The canal makes the city the port of the interior.

title: The First Street Railway
description: The New York and Harlem Railroad starts horse-drawn cars on rails along the Bowery from Prince Street to 14th Street.

title: City of Brooklyn
description: The village and town of Brooklyn are incorporated as a city, soon the third largest in the country.

title: The Great Fire of 1835
description: In a freezing gale a fire burns seventeen blocks and between 530 and 700 buildings east of Broad Street, including the Merchants' Exchange.

title: Croton Water
description: The city celebrates the Croton Aqueduct, which brings river water 41 miles to a receiving reservoir in the future Central Park and a distributing reservoir at 42nd Street.

title: The Great Fire of 1845
description: A fire and a saltpeter explosion destroy 345 buildings around Broad Street and kill thirty people.

title: High Bridge
description: The aqueduct bridge that carries Croton water over the Harlem River is completed; it is the oldest bridge standing in the city.

title: The Crystal Palace
description: The Exhibition of the Industry of All Nations opens in an iron-and-glass hall on Reservoir Square; the building burns in October 1858.

title: Central Park Authorized
description: The legislature sets aside more than 700 acres in the middle of Manhattan for a park.

title: Castle Garden
description: The old fort off the Battery opens as the Emigrant Landing Depot; more than eight million immigrants pass through before 1890.

title: Seneca Village Cleared
description: Seneca Village, a settlement of about 225 people founded by free Black landowners, and the other homes on the park site are cleared as construction of Central Park begins.

title: The Greensward Plan
description: Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux win the Central Park design competition; the first section opens to skaters that December.

title: The First Elevated
description: Charles T. Harvey's West Side and Yonkers Patent Railway demonstrates a cable-hauled elevated line above Greenwich Street; regular service begins in 1870 and it grows into the Ninth Avenue El.

title: New York Crosses the Harlem
description: The city annexes the Westchester towns of Kingsbridge, West Farms and Morrisania, the western Bronx.

title: The Els Go Uptown
description: The Sixth Avenue elevated opens, followed in August by the Third Avenue line; steam trains reach Harlem by 1880 and open upper Manhattan to building.

title: Brooklyn Bridge
description: The East River bridge opens after fourteen years of work; its 1,595-foot span is the longest in the world.

title: Statue of Liberty
description: Liberty Enlightening the World is dedicated on Bedloe's Island.

title: The World Building
description: The New York World Building on Park Row is completed at 309 feet, the first building to rise above Trinity's spire. It is demolished in 1955.

title: Ellis Island
description: The federal immigration station opens on Ellis Island, which is enlarged with fill from about 3 to 27 acres; some twelve million people enter through it by 1954.

title: Brooklyn Fills Kings County
description: The City of Brooklyn annexes the towns of Flatbush, Gravesend and New Utrecht, and Flatlands in 1896, taking in all of Kings County.

title: Harlem River Ship Canal
description: The canal through the northern tip of Manhattan opens, cutting Marble Hill off from the island; eleven days earlier the city annexed the Bronx east of the Bronx River.

title: Greater New York
description: New York, Brooklyn, western Queens County, Staten Island and the Bronx are consolidated into one city of five boroughs and 3.4 million people.

title: Flatiron Building
description: The 22-story Fuller Building is completed on the triangle at 23rd Street.

title: Williamsburg Bridge
description: The second East River bridge opens with the longest suspension span in the world, 1,600 feet.

title: The Subway
description: The Interborough Rapid Transit opens from City Hall to 145th Street and Broadway, 9 miles and 28 stations.

title: Under the Rivers
description: Subway trains reach Brooklyn through the Joralemon Street Tunnel, the first under the East River; the Hudson and Manhattan tubes from Hoboken open the next month.

title: Singer Tower
description: The 612-foot Singer Building becomes the world's tallest building, passed a year later by the 700-foot Metropolitan Life tower. The Singer is demolished in 1968.

title: Queensboro Bridge
description: The cantilever bridge over Blackwell's Island opens Queens to Manhattan; the Manhattan Bridge follows at the end of the year.

title: Pennsylvania Station
description: The Pennsylvania Railroad opens its station by McKim, Mead & White with tunnels under the Hudson and East rivers.

title: Grand Central Terminal
description: The new terminal opens over two levels of electrified tracks; the covered rail yard to the north becomes Park Avenue.

title: Woolworth Building
description: The 792-foot Woolworth Building opens, the tallest building in the world until 1930.

title: The Zoning Resolution
description: The city adopts the country's first citywide zoning law; its setback rules shape the stepped towers of the 1920s.

title: Hell Gate Bridge
description: The New York Connecting Railroad's steel arch, the longest in the world at 977 feet, opens between Queens and Wards Island.

title: Holland Tunnel
description: The first mechanically ventilated vehicle tunnel under the Hudson opens between Canal Street and Jersey City.

title: Staten Island's Bridges
description: The Goethals Bridge and the Outerbridge Crossing open to New Jersey, the first road bridges to Staten Island.

title: Chrysler Building
description: The 1,046-foot Chrysler Building opens as the tallest building in the world.

title: Empire State Building
description: The 1,250-foot Empire State Building opens; it is the world's tallest building until 1970.

title: Floyd Bennett Field
description: The city dedicates its first municipal airport on filled marsh at Barren Island.

title: George Washington Bridge
description: The Hudson River bridge opens to traffic with a 3,500-foot span, nearly twice the previous record.

title: Rockefeller Center
description: The RCA Building opens at the centre of a complex of fourteen buildings built between 1930 and 1939.

title: Triborough Bridge
description: Robert Moses's complex of three bridges joins Manhattan, the Bronx and Queens across Randalls and Wards islands.

title: The West Side Improvement
description: The Henry Hudson Parkway is completed along the Hudson and the New York Central's tracks are roofed over by an enlarged Riverside Park. The Lincoln Tunnel opens the same year.

title: The World of Tomorrow
description: The World's Fair opens on Flushing Meadows, until then the Corona ash dumps; the Bronx–Whitestone Bridge opened the day before.

title: LaGuardia Airport
description: New York Municipal Airport opens to airlines on filled land at North Beach in Queens.

title: Belt Parkway
description: The parkway around the shore of Brooklyn and Queens opens; the Queens–Midtown Tunnel follows on 15 November.

title: Stuyvesant Town
description: The first tenants move into Metropolitan Life's Stuyvesant Town, built over eighteen blocks of the Gas House District.

title: Fresh Kills
description: The city begins filling the tidal marsh of Fresh Kills on Staten Island with refuse; it grows into the largest landfill in the world before closing in March 2001.

title: Idlewild
description: New York International Airport opens on the marshes of Jamaica Bay; it is renamed for John F. Kennedy in December 1963.

title: Brooklyn–Battery Tunnel
description: The longest continuous underwater road tunnel in North America opens between the Battery and Red Hook.

title: United Nations
description: The General Assembly Building opens beside the Secretariat (1950), completing the United Nations headquarters on eighteen acres of former slaughterhouses at Turtle Bay.

title: Last Train on Third Avenue
description: The Third Avenue elevated, the last in Manhattan, closes south of 149th Street and is pulled down.

title: Cross Bronx Expressway
description: The first sections of Robert Moses's expressway open; cut through built-up neighbourhoods and displacing thousands of residents, the road is finished across the borough in 1963.

title: Lincoln Center
description: President Eisenhower breaks ground for Lincoln Center on the cleared blocks of San Juan Hill; Philharmonic Hall opens in September 1962.

title: Penn Station Demolished
description: Demolition of Pennsylvania Station begins; Madison Square Garden opens on the site in 1968.

title: The 1964 World's Fair
description: A second fair opens at Flushing Meadows around the Unisphere.

title: Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge
description: The bridge across the Narrows opens with the world's longest suspension span, 4,260 feet, tying Staten Island to the rest of the city.

title: The Landmarks Law
description: Mayor Robert F. Wagner Jr. signs the law creating the Landmarks Preservation Commission, a response to losses like Penn Station.

title: Co-op City
description: The first residents move into Co-op City in the northeast Bronx; with 15,372 apartments it is the largest cooperative housing development in the world.

title: World Trade Center
description: The Port Authority dedicates the World Trade Center; the 110-story twin towers are briefly the tallest buildings in the world.

title: The West Side Highway Falls
description: A section of the elevated West Side Highway collapses near Gansevoort Street; the road is closed and taken down between 1977 and 1989.

title: Battery Park City
description: Landfill for Battery Park City, 92 acres made partly from the World Trade Center excavation, is completed in the Hudson; the first apartments open in 1982.

title: September 11
description: Hijacked airliners destroy the twin towers; most of the 2,977 victims of the day's attacks die here.

title: The High Line
description: The first section of the park on the disused West Side freight viaduct opens between Gansevoort and 20th streets.

title: Hurricane Sandy
description: A record storm tide of nearly 14 feet at the Battery floods the shores of all five boroughs, subway tunnels and the power network; more than forty people die in the city.

title: One World Trade Center
description: One World Trade Center opens at 1,776 feet, the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere.

title: Second Avenue Subway
description: The first phase of the Second Avenue Subway opens with stations at 72nd, 86th and 96th streets.

title: Hudson Yards
description: The first phase of Hudson Yards opens on a platform over the West Side rail yard.

title: Moynihan Train Hall
description: A new hall for Penn Station opens in the 1914 James A. Farley Post Office across Eighth Avenue.
